investment_theses.thesis: I-bond yield at 5.51% creates tactical float into USDC/stablecoin yields (30-90 day horizon); crowded tech capex cycle creates rotation into consumer staples and defensives (chocolate, candy inflation play).
supporting_signals: Treasury announces I-bond rate 5.51% through April 2027 (new floor for risk-free yield)
CNBC: Cramer pivots to consumer staples, away from AI tech
CNBC: Cocoa and sugar inflation fueling candy price hikes (Hershey pinch)
Meta given negative S&P outlook on capex concerns, signaling tech spending cycle peak
investment_theses.counter_view: Inflation expectations may rise and push I-bond yields even higher, making 5.51% a temporary floor, not anchor; consumer staples are crowded rotation trade and likely priced in by options market.
investment_theses.expression: Long USDC yield farming at 12-18 mo. duration; long consumer staples ETF (XLP) vs. short Nasdaq-100 (QQQ); long cocoa futures (ICE) or Hershey (HSY) calls; short Meta (META) equity or long META put spreads.
